_about: PRODUCTS.JSON — the content contract for the /p/{campaign} product landings. The kit's rule is that copy lives in data, not components: machine/campaign.js renders this file and holds no product words of its own. Every line here is lifted from reference/companies/README.md (official taglines, descriptions, feature lines, FAQ copy, proof points and attributed testimonials) and every asset path is a file that exists under /assets/img/companies/. data/campaigns.json still owns the agent panel — the opener, the chips and the pending_positioning note come from there, never from here.
_honesty: These are real third-party brands, real published claims and real named people. Nothing in proof[] or quote{} is a Stagwell.AI measurement: every figure carries proofSource and every quote carries source, and campaign.js renders both. Where a brand's own line has no named speaker we say so rather than borrowing a face for it. Where the kit supplies no asset, a visible [PLACEHOLDER] stays.

_schema.accent: the product's own brand hue — hairlines, numerals, small marks, the lockup band
_schema.accentInk: ink proven legible on a solid fill of accent (>= 4.5:1 for body, >= 3:1 for display)
_schema.lockup.ink: ink for the LOCKUP BAND, which is often not the accent fill — Machine OS's band is its logo's own black, whose ink is white, while ink on its orange accent is black. lockup.pillInk overrides it for the category pill where a gradient band makes one colour work at one end and not the other.
_schema.accentNote: why THIS hex, out of the several the README lists
_schema.band: the deep surface the proof strip and lockup sit on; bandInk / bandFigure are its text and numeral colours
_schema.tint: a wash of accent light enough to carry the icon sets, which are all solid-colour-on-transparent
_schema.heroKind: image = a real photograph/still · mark = the official logo mark as art · diagram = an official explanatory graphic (must be captioned + sourced) · gradient = the brand's own signature gradient, no borrowed picture
_schema.shots[].frame: every supplied screenshot is cut out on black, so all frames are dark
_schema.valueProps[].icon: null where the kit ships no icon for that product — those cards go text/number-led

We lead with the CES orange because that is the kit we were actually handed — logo.png is the orange mark on black and hero.jpg is orange light on charcoal, so the navy set would fight every image on the page. Ink on the orange is black, not white: white gives 3.4:1 and fails, black gives 6.1:1.

products.summary: Lifelike voice and chat agents for sales, support, retention, payments and feedback — 24/7, in any language. They adapt in real time to customer history, context and intent, and plug into Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe and Make. Built in Agent Studio, no code required.
products.accentNote: Sky #159CBD and Mint #57BF94 come from the NewVoices Brand Book v1.0, which the README marks authoritative over the older site teal #0D9488. Sky is the darker of the pair so it takes the accent role. Its ink is the brand's own Ink #16181A, not white — white on Sky is 3.2:1 and fails, Ink is 5.5:1. Deep bands are set on Ink rather than Sky for the same reason.

lockup.note: The Brand Book's signature Sky→Mint gradient at 90°, carrying the white lockup — the brand's own pairing — but WEIGHTED. A straight two-stop ramp puts the tail of the white wordmark on Mint at 2.3:1, under the 3:1 a graphical object needs; holding Sky to 58% keeps the whole lockup on Sky (3.2:1) and lets Mint run out behind the category pill, which takes brand Ink instead of white (5.5:1 on Sky, 7.9:1 on Mint). Same two brand colours, same direction, legible at both ends.

products.heroNote: The kit ships no NewVoices hero image, and its one product visual earns its place lower down under “Inside the product”. Rather than pad the hero with a decorative gradient slab, the column runs lockup → headline → summary and lets the agent panel keep the fold.
